name: Kinabalian
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Kaufman, Daniel & Nikolaus Himmelmann. Suprasegmental phonology (Philippine/western Austronesian survey chapter); Zorc, R. David. 1993. Overview of Austronesian and Philippine accent patterns (OL Special Publication 24: 17-24).
sources.note: No entry for Kinabalian/Cabalian (grep Cabal/Kabal/Leyte/Waray: nothing relevant).

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David Paul. 1977. The Bisayan dialects of the Philippines: subgrouping and reconstruction. Pacific Linguistics C-44. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Kinabalian/Cabalian is NOT among Zorc's 36 sampled Bisayan dialects (no hit for Cabalian, San Juan, or a Southern Leyte Warayan point). Sec. 3.1.3 'Accent' gives only the family-level statement: all Bisayan dialects except Kuyonon and Tausug have an accentual system with length on an accented open penult, and 'stems or derivatives with a closed penult... are accented on the penult' -- not a statement about Kinabalian.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David (comp.). Working list 'Jason William Lobel PUBLICATIONS' (zorc.net/RDZorc/Lobel=JasonLobel/), plus zorc.net RDZorc folder listings (Waray, Baybayanon=Utudnon, Porohanon=Camotes, Bantayanon, WORDLISTS, PUBLICATIONS, GCP, Subgrouping.FIVE, r-d(errors-Bisayan))
sources.note: No Kinabalian-specific paper by Lobel listed; no Kinabalian/Cabalian field-data bundle in Zorc's open archive (SEAlang Zorc menu 'Leyte' bundle is Cebuano of Leyte).

sources.citation: Gorme, Emmanuel, et al. 2026. Language politics and identity: the shift from Kinabalian to Cebuano among the Cabalianon of San Juan, Southern Leyte. World Education Connect Multidisciplinary e-Publication 6(1): 666-678. doi:10.65494/pinagpalapublishing.122
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic interview study of language shift; cites Lobel 2013 and the ISO request only.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Kabalian language'; Wikipedia (tl) 'Wikang Kabalian' (raw wikitext, fetched sources 2026-09-17)
sources.note: No phonology section and no references; vocabulary tables carry a few accent marks (idò 'dog', idíng 'cat', bayáy 'house') but no statement.

sources.citation: Cruzada, Metchie C. & Mark B. Galdo. 2023. Siyasat-Suri sa Binisayang Silagonhon at Binisayang Cabalianon ng Timog Leyte: Isang deskriptibong paglalarawan. International Journal of Research Studies in Education 12(4): 31-41. doi:10.5861/ijrse.2023.2004 (in Filipino).
sources.note: No stress statement. Glossary-based comparison of Silago and San Juan Bisaya; notes Cabalianon /y/ for Cebuano /l/ (bawod~bayud, buwak~buyak) and syllable additions (bay~bayay, su~suyo) (p.37); 'tono, diin' (tone, stress) of San Juan speech mentioned only impressionistically as 'different' (p.33).

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. hdl:10125/101972 (Glottolog ref 317908)
sources.note: Nothing for Kinabalian. Kinabalian appears only at p.3 (listed among 'previously-undocumented languages' Lobel documented), Map 1.8 key c12 (p.24), p.41 (mu- instead of <um>), p.43 (Warayan outlier lacking distinct present/future verb forms, like Porohanon/Baybayanon), p.83 ('Cabalin-on' shares the Surigaonon *y > /j/ shift), p.365 (heavy lexical borrowing). No Kinabalian forms cited; the dissertation's only accent statements concern Manide/Inagta Alabat (8.2.9, p.259) and Mindanao languages (fn.3 p.287).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2009. Change Request 2009-084 (requester Jason Lobel, supporter William Hall): create [cbw] Kinabalian; with 'Request for New Language Code Element' form.
sources.note: Nothing. States the language 'was only discovered by Lobel in 2006', Warayan branch of Central Bisayan, contact language with Cebuano/Surigaonon elements, ~14,000 speakers in six barangays of San Juan (Cabalian); published sources cited are only Zorc 1975/1977 and Lobel's dissertation in preparation.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2025. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 28th ed., entry Kinabalian [cbw]. Dallas: SIL International.
